title: Reduce pager fatigue by implementing tiered burn-rate thresholds and alert suppression
creator: Priya Nair
description: Follow-up to the Feb 8 capacity regression that produced a sustained SLO breach and an excessive number of pager escalations. The root cause analysis shows two compounding issues: (1) a conservative global burn-rate alert fired for multiple clusters simultaneously, and (2) lack of tiered paging rules caused informational alerts to escalate to on-call. This ticket collects action items to reduce paging noise, introduce tiered burn thresholds, and create guardrails so regressions degrade gracefully without unnecessary wakeups.
comments: 2026-02-10: Initial postmortem published (link in links). Triage meeting: agreed goal is to reduce pagers from this class of incidents by >= 70% while preserving time-to-detect for high-severity customer-impacting outages.

2026-02-11: Decided on a two-layer approach: adjust burn-rate thresholds (global -> regional -> critical-path) and add a short-term suppression window for repeated identical signals. Engineering to prototype threshold changes on staging first.

2026-02-12: Design review with SRE and Platform teams. Trade-offs discussed: wider thresholds reduce noise but increase time-to-detect; mitigation: create critical-path detectors that always page and informational detectors that post to slack/console only.
2026-02-13: Marco implemented alert dedupe and cooldown in a feature branch (PR link in links). Preliminary end-to-end tests show 4x reduction in duplicate pagers for synthetic bursts.
2026-02-14: PM review (Aisha Cheng) requested clearer runbook updates and a dashboard tile showing pre/post pager counts by alert class for the next 30 days. Added to action items.
action_items: AI-1: Implement tiered burn-rate thresholds: global warning (50% burn in 1h, no pager), regional critical (80% burn in 30m, page SRE). Owner: Marco Alvarez. Due: 2026-02-21.
AI-2: Add deduplication + 10m cooldown for repeated identical burn alerts to prevent immediate re-paging. Owner: SRE team (lead: Samira Bose). Due: 2026-02-18.
AI-3: Create a critical-path detector set (latency and error budget for customer-facing routes) that always escalates to on-call. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-02-20.
AI-4: Update runbooks to document paging policy, suppression rules, and manual override steps for major incidents. Owner: Runbook Owning Group (DOCS: @Elena Park). Due: 2026-02-24.
AI-5: Instrument Grafana dashboards with a 'pager signal-to-noise' chart and add a retention view showing counts before/after changes. Owner: Observability team (lead: Jonas Kim). Due: 2026-02-28.
AI-6: Add automated tests that generate synthetic bursts to validate suppression/dedup behavior in staging nightly. Owner: QE (lead: Miguel Torres). Due: 2026-02-25.
AI-7: Re-evaluate SLO slices to separate internal infra SLOs from customer-facing SLOs to avoid internal noise causing customer-facing pagers. Owner: Product SRE (lead: Aisha Cheng). Due: 2026-03-05.
AI-8: Run a 30-day monitoring and compare pager counts, SLO latency regressions, and mean time to detect. Deliver a short report. Owner: Marco Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-30.
AI-9: Create a small training doc for on-call engineers describing new paging tiers and where to escalate if suppression hides an event. Owner: On-call trainer (Tom Reed). Due: 2026-02-23.
